statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: Neutral: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting may be implicated, but the facts do not identify a financial institution, a SAR filing obligation, or a failure to report.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates suspicious activity reporting by a “financial institution” (as defined/implemented by Treasury regulations) when the institution detects suspicious transactions, and provides related protections (e.g., safe harbor and confidentiality). Here, the fact pattern describes Entity SYN_e2418bd1 (a business customer) sending/receiving several large wires, including one noted as “trade-finance over-invoiced,” which could be suspicious. However, § 5318(g) applies to the reporting duties of a covered financial institution, not directly to the customer’s conduct, and the facts do not state (i) which bank/financial institution processed these wires, (ii) whether that institution is subject to SAR rules under § 5318(g), or (iii) whether a SAR was required and not filed (or was filed). Therefore, while § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting could be triggered by these transactions, the provided facts are insufficient to determine applicability to any obligated reporter.
